edges.description: The abnormal SPACR is deposited into the matrix, where it disrupts normal matrix assembly around photoreceptor outer segments.
The matrix holds outer segments in alignment; a disorganized matrix lets the outer segments lose alignment and shorten.
A defective matrix is proposed to impair handling of shed outer-segment material by the RPE, leaving autofluorescent material in the subretinal space.
Shortened rod and cone outer segments in embryonic retina.
edges.limitations: Transient knockdown reduces impg1 rather than expressing the human dominant allele, so it models loss of SPACR, not the dominant-negative behavior of a heterozygous mutant protein; it reports outer-segment length only and not the adult-onset course or the vitelliform lesion.

edges.description: Autofluorescent hyperreflective deposits form between outer segments and RPE.
edges.limitations: Mice have no macula, so the deposits are scattered across the fundus rather than forming a single central vitelliform lesion, and the knockout removes SPACR rather than expressing the human dominant allele.

nodes.description: Constitutive Impg1 knockout with no detectable retinal SPACR. From 9 months, autofluorescent subretinal deposits across the fundus, falling scotopic and photopic ERG amplitudes, outer retinal thinning, disorganized IPM and outer segments, and RPE damage. Because it removes SPACR rather than expressing a mutant allele, it models the matrix-loss consequence shared by both IMPG1 diseases, not the dominant-negative allele itself.

evidence.reference_title: SPACR Encoded by IMPG1 Is Essential for Photoreceptor Survival by Interplaying between the Interphotoreceptor Matrix and the Retinal Pigment Epithelium.
evidence.snippet: Impg1-/- mice provide a novel model for mechanistic investigations and the development of therapies for VMD and RP caused by IMPG1 pathogenic variants.

nodes.description: SPACR is made by rod and cone photoreceptors and, with SPACRCAN (IMPG2), supplies most of the chondroitin sulfate of the interphotoreceptor matrix and the cone-specific glycocalyx. An abnormal or reduced-function SPACR disturbs the organization of the matrix around the outer segments; loss of IMPG1 in mice removes chondroitin sulfate and the cone PNA glycocalyx from the outer-segment compartment and, in older animals, leaves the matrix vacuolated and disorganized.

evidence.reference_title: Expression and characterization of the IPM 150 gene (IMPG1) product, a novel human photoreceptor cell-associated chondroitin-sulfate proteoglycan.
evidence.snippet: In situ hybridization analyses indicate that, in the eye, IPM 150 mRNA is expressed specifically by cone and rod photoreceptor cells.

evidence.reference_title: Proteoglycan IMPG2 Shapes the Interphotoreceptor Matrix and Modulates Vision.
evidence.snippet: In normal retina, IMPG1 and IMPG2 occupy distinct IPM compartments, represent the main source of chondroitin sulfate and are fundamental for the constitution of the cone-specific glycocalyx stained by the PNA (peanut agglutinin) lectin marker.

evidence.reference_title: Extracellular matrix component expression in human pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal organoids recapitulates retinogenesis in vivo and reveals an important role for IMPG1 and CD44 in the development of photoreceptors and interphotoreceptor matrix.
evidence.snippet: Blocking the action of CD44 and IMPG1 in pluripotent stem cell derived retinal organoids affected the development of photoreceptors, their inner/outer segments and connecting cilia and disrupted IPM formation, with IMPG1 having an earlier and more significant impact.

nodes.description: A heterozygous IMPG1 allele produces an abnormal SPACR protein that acts in the interphotoreceptor matrix despite a normal allele. The prototypical change p.Leu238Arg sits at the start of the conserved N-terminal SEA1 domain; structural modeling predicts it destabilizes SEA1, but the mutant protein is produced at normal levels and is not mislocalized, so it is not a null allele. The founding study proposes a dominant-negative effect, the mutant behaving abnormally inside the extracellular matrix, which separates this disease from the recessive IMPG1 disease, where a single null allele is non-penetrant. A second codon-238 missense change (p.Leu238Pro) and the perifoveal-maculopathy change p.Leu579Pro are also heterozygous.

nodes.description: Autofluorescent, hyperreflective material accumulates between the photoreceptor outer segments and the RPE. In patients this forms the central vitelliform lesion; in Impg1 knockout mice, which lack a macula, equivalent autofluorescent deposits appear across the fundus with age. In IMPG1 disease the material sits above the RPE, unlike BEST1 disease, where it lies between the RPE and Bruch's membrane.
